o: A special number is a palindrome where digit d appears exactly d times (so digit 0 never appears). Given n up to 1e15, find the smallest special number strictly greater than n. Examples: 2 → 22, 33 → 212. The total digit count of any special number is the sum of a subset of {1..9}; numbers relevant here have at most 17 digits, so we can precompute ALL special numbers up to that length and binary search.
k: Choose a subset S of digits 1..9 with total count ≤ 17; the palindrome is determined by arranging half of each digit's copies around an optional center.
If the total count is odd, exactly one chosen digit must be odd (it supplies the middle digit); if even, all chosen digits must be even.
Enumerate distinct permutations of the half-multiset (small), build each palindrome, collect, sort, and bisect for the answer.

a.n: Approach 1: Generate All Special Numbers + Binary Search
a.i: There are only 2^9 subsets, and half-multisets have at most 8 elements, so the total number of distinct palindromes is modest (thousands). Generating them all once and binary-searching answers any n instantly.
s: For each subset of {1..9} with digit-sum ≤ 17: build the half multiset (d//2 copies of d).
Check parity: odd total requires exactly one odd digit (the center); even total requires none.
For each distinct permutation of the half, form the palindrome half + center + reversed half and record it.
Sort all generated numbers; return the first strictly greater than n via bisect_right.
a.t: Precomputation: 2^9 subsets × at most a few hundred distinct half-permutations each — well under a millisecond-scale workload; queries are O(log |specials|).

w: Why sum ≤ 17 suffices: n has at most 16 digits, and a 17-digit special number always exceeds any 16-digit n. Pitfalls: forgetting the parity condition linking the center digit to odd counts, generating duplicate palindromes across permutations (use a set), and 64-bit parsing for 17-digit values. Follow-up: count special numbers in a range, or find the k-th smallest special number.
